title: Power Stack Daily Research Refresh
regime: Mixed: global capital scarcity/rates remain dominant, while the verified US-China truce extension through 10 January 2027 removes the immediate tariff cliff and reduces one goods-inflation/corporate-uncertainty tail risk.
whatIsNewNow: US and China extended the trade truce through 10 January 2027. This is a real easing in near-term tariff tail risk, but the summit still has to resolve or narrow disputes over rare earths, advanced technology/AI controls, Chinese purchases and broader trade terms.
Japan's 10Y JGB printed about 3.075%, the highest since August 1996. Together with US 10Y yields around 5%+, this strengthens the global-duration/capital-scarcity regime.
September US flash Composite PMI remains 58.4, with manufacturing 57.0 and services 58.7; strong activity and price pressure keep the Fed/rates hurdle high.
Asia crude imports recovered to about 23.96mbpd, a post-war high, but remain roughly 13% below the pre-war average. Logistics are improving without fully normalising.
Gold is around the low-$4,280s and remains tactically dominated by real yields and the dollar rather than geopolitical hedging.
SoftBank's $11.1B bond financing for OpenAI reinforces the split between strong-sponsor funding access and a harsher financing environment for weaker AI/project-finance structures.

For equities, the summit is most directly relevant to semiconductors/AI hardware, China-exposed companies and critical-mineral supply chains; do not treat a positive headline as broad risk-on without rates/breadth confirmation.
